Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation
articles.abstract: Abstract Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial–immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB–Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

articles.title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
articles.abstract: Abstract Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri ; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter . Related megabase-scale plasmids were detected in at least 400 infant and adult gut, and other microbiomes. Diverse Enterobacteriaceae hosts, conjugation machinery, and DNA modification patterns suggest that these elements are self-transmissible, with a broad host range. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Overall, the vast plasmid coding capacity may broaden host range, increase competitiveness, control invasion by other elements, and counter programmed cell death.

articles.title: Author Correction: Ecdysone signaling-induced dumpless1 expression controls nurse cell dumping in Drosophila oogenesis
G-quadruplex structures affect the immune response to bacterial infection in mouse macrophages
articles.abstract: Abstract Macrophages orchestrate immunity via transcriptional reprogramming, largely controlled by the master regulator NF-κB. However, mechanisms of promoter selection remain enigmatic. Here, we reveal that DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s) modulate the macrophage transcriptome during inflammation. By investigating the G4 ligand pyridostatin (PDS) in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, we establish that G4 stabilization significantly decreases the inflammatory response without affecting mitochondrial metabolism or pathogen clearance. Instead, NF-κB-dependent transcription of activation markers and proinflammatory cytokines is selectively repressed. Using chromatin accessibility profiling, NF-κB ChIP, and in silico predictions, we demonstrate that G4 stabilization sterically hinders NF-κB promoter occupancy. Furthermore, PDS stabilizes transient, transcription-induced G4s, prematurely shutting down transcription and reverting local chromatin to a dormant state. Thus, G4 formation represents a potential strategy to modulate dysregulated macrophage activation.

articles.title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

articles.title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
articles.abstract: Abstract Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX 2 , previously reported as having inverted S 1 -T 1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX 2 show anti-Kasha S 0 ←S 2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S 0 →S 1 , linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S 0 →S 2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S 0 ←S 1 emission, whereas exciting S 0 →S 1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S 2 and S 1 is very weak, S 2 -T N intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S 1 ↔T 1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T 1 →S 1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

articles.title: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury
Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
articles.abstract: Abstract Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

articles.title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
articles.abstract: Abstract Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

articles.title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
articles.abstract: Abstract Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

articles.title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction
Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
articles.abstract: Abstract Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting Braf V600E - or Braf ΔN -expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. Braf V600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than Braf ΔN . Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.

articles.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
articles.abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China’s food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance ( gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes ( qnrB17 , qnrS1 ) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes ( bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

articles.title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset

60 Years of Biogeochemistry
and Remediation Science
Issue Publication Information

Depth-Independent
Soil Organic Carbon Persistence
across Climate Gradients in Coastal Wetlands
articles.abstract: Abstract Coastal wetland soils constitute a major global blue carbon pool. Yet, how soil organic carbon (SOC) persistence varies with soil depth and responds to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we assessed depth-related patterns and climatic controls on SOC persistence using radiocarbon (Δ14C) measurements from 82 samples across 41 sites spanning temperate to tropical coastal wetlands. Radiocarbon-inferred SOC persistence did not differ significantly between topsoil (0–10 cm) and subsoil (40–60 cm) across climate zones and wetland types, with mean Δ14C values of −179.0 ± 155.5‰ and −200.9 ± 161.8‰, respectively (p > 0.05). Interactions among climate, vegetation, and soil biogeochemistry explained about 55% of the variation in SOC persistence in both topsoil and subsoil. Both layers exhibited comparable sensitivity to mean annual temperature and precipitation. However, the inferred regulatory pathways differed between soil layers, with stronger direct climatic effects in topsoil and greater indirect mediation through soil physicochemical and mineral-associated processes in subsoil. Across spatial climatic gradients, higher mean annual temperature and precipitation were associated with greater SOC accumulation but lower persistence, suggesting a potential trade-off between SOC quantity and persistence. These findings demonstrate limited vertical differentiation in SOC persistence between the 0–10 cm and 40–60 cm layers and highlight the need to better represent depth-specific regulatory processes in carbon-climate feedback frameworks.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Warming Patterns
Shape Divergent Multilevel Physiological
Responses and Underlying Metabolic Mechanisms in Aquatic Organisms
articles.abstract: Abstract Although the impacts of global warming on aquatic ecosystems are widely recognized, the biological consequences of distinct warming patterns remain largely unknown. We investigated physiological and metabolic responses of Daphnia magna, Chironomus kiiensis, and zebrafish under constant warming (+1, +3 °C), heatwave, and temperature fluctuation. Dynamic patterns exhibited stronger physiological responses, with mean absolute effect sizes across survival, growth, development, behavior, and stress functional categories following the order heatwave > fluctuation > +3 °C > +1 °C. Response profiles varied among warming patterns: constant +3 °C induced moderate and broad changes across biochemical stress, developmental, and behavioral end points; heatwave accelerated zebrafish hatching and C. kiiensis pupation while increasing deformity, suppressing growth, and elevating mortality; and fluctuation induced pronounced biochemical stress responses, particularly HSP70, together with developmental disruption, while producing weaker survival and growth effects than heatwave. Across taxa, dominant response profiles differed, with broad multiend point disruption in D. magna, stress-dominant responses in C. kiiensis, and developmental sensitivity in zebrafish. Metabolomic analysis further identified warming-pattern-specific metabolic signatures associated with energy metabolism under +3 °C, membrane-related processes under heatwave, and redox-related processes under fluctuation. Together, these findings provide a scientific basis for improving aquatic ecological risk assessment under increasingly variable warming scenarios.

articles.title:
Psychoactive
Pollutant
Impacts Baseline Immune Traits
but Not Behavior and Microbiome in a Fish
articles.abstract: Abstract Pharmaceutical pollution is an increasing global threat to freshwater ecosystems. Psychoactive drugs, such as antidepressants, are of particular concern because they affect evolutionarily conserved neuroendocrine pathways in nontarget organisms. As these pathways regulate interconnected biological systems, understanding the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical exposure requires an integrative approach. Here, we investigated the effects of 28-day exposure to control (freshwater), low (4.2 ± 0.3 ng/L), and high (637.5 ± 173.84 ng/L) fluoxetine concentrations on behaviors, baseline immune traits, and skin mucus microbiome composition in the Murray River rainbowfish (Melanotaenia fluviatilis). Fluoxetine exposure did not impact fish behavior, including activity, freezing behavior, shelter use, or microbiome composition. In contrast, immune traits were significantly altered. Both fluoxetine concentrations reduced total white blood cell (WBC) count, while only fish exposed to the low concentration showed reduced lymphocyte counts and elevated neutrophil counts, consistent with a stress-associated WBC redistribution response. Our findings show that different, but interconnected, biological systems can differ in their sensitivity to pollutants and suggest that immune traits may be an early, sensitive indicator of exposure to psychoactive pharmaceuticals. These findings highlight the importance of integrating multiple biological end points to obtain a more comprehensive understanding of the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical contamination.

on “Kidney Urate

Substances and their Alternatives and Uric Acid Levels: Evidence from
a Case–Control Study and an Animal Study”

Divergent Responses
of Manganese Oxides to Olivine
Dissolution and Their Control on Trace Metal Fates under an Ocean
Alkalinity Enhancement Scenario
articles.abstract: Abstract Olivine-based ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a promising carbon dioxide removal technology; however, the geochemical fate of olivine-derived toxic metals, particularly nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr) at marine sediment interfaces, remains poorly constrained. We employed dialysis-membrane microcosms to isolate olivine from Mn oxides, allowing only dissolved species to diffuse and react under three olivine loadings (1, 5, and 10 g L–1) in seawater for 60 days. Results revealed that (1) Ni was preferentially sequestered by the Mn oxides, with δ-MnO2 showing higher uptake capacity than birnessite, (2) Cr was co-sequestered with secondary Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides rather than adsorbing directly onto Mn oxides, and (3) synergistic Ni2+ isomorphic substitution and Fe(II)-driven Mn(III) reduction rearranged δ-MnO2 into a more stable hexagonal layered framework. Consequently, both δ-MnO2 and birnessite act as long-term Ni sinks, preventing Ni remobilization via desorption or diagenetic phase transitions. These findings support a proposed “spatial decoupling” OAE strategy, where olivine is pre-dissolved in land- or ship-based reactors to remove Cr via Fe co-precipitation. Subsequent discharge of the Ni-bearing alkaline effluent into shallow coastal regions allows benthic Mn oxides to scavenge Ni, reducing toxicity risks associated with direct mineral contact.

articles.title:
Parenteral Nutrition
as a Source of Xenobiotic Exposure
in Preterm Infants in a Single-Center Case Study
articles.abstract: Abstract In premature infants, successful ex utero maturation depends on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Chemical insults during this period may impact long-term development. Given immature hepatic biotransformation, parenteral xenobiotic exposure may be of particular toxicological relevance. We conducted a single-center case study to characterize the xenobiotic burden of neonatal parenteral nutrition (PN). A standardized PN regimen for a 28-week, 1000 g reference infant was passed through infusion lines and the flow-through analyzed via a multianalyte exposome LC-MS/MS assay. Eighteen of 221 targeted xenobiotics were detected. Diisononyl phthalate (DINP, 780 ng/mL), bisphenol A (BPA, 250 ng/mL), methylparaben (MP, 74 ng/mL), and 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanoic acid (HMFA, 43 ng/mL) showed the highest mean concentrations. The estimated daily intake of BPA (9.5 μg/kg bw/d) exceeded calculated and official Health-Based Guidance Values. Consistent with immature detoxification, pharmacokinetic modeling suggested accumulation of DINP, MINP, and free BPA in premature infants. The higher predicted exposure of premature infants to free BPA warrants investigation into 4-methyl-2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)pent-1-ene (MBP) formation under potentially saturated Phase II metabolism. An exploratory analysis of plasma data from extremely premature infants indicated PN as a contributory rather than predominant source of intervention-related exposure. These findings represent a relevant clinical reference scenario rather than a population-wide exposure estimate.

articles.title: Fe3 + Activation of Metal Sulfides for High-Performance Mercury Removal from Nonferrous Smelting Gas: A Dual Mercury Adsorption Mechanism
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric elemental mercury (Hg0) emitted from the nonferrous metallurgy industry poses severe risks to ecosystems. Although metal sulfides are promising in Hg0 adsorption under high-concentration SO2 conditions, they typically suffer from poor performance at elevated temperatures due to weak binding affinity. Herein, a trivalent iron (Fe3+) activation strategy to boost Hg0 adsorption activity of metal sulfides was developed for the first time, which leverages electron-deficient Fe3+ to induce electronic reconstruction. This Fe3+ activation strategy is applicable to various metal sulfides, generating Fe sites with high activity and stability. Among the various candidates, the Fe3+-activated MoS2 delivers a record-theoretical saturated Hg0 adsorption capacity of 69.56 mg·g–1 at 150 °C, which is 4.35 times higher than that of pristine MoS2. The sulfur vacancies on MoS2 serve as the key anchoring sites for Fe3+, generating stable single-atom, dimer, and trimer Fe configurations. These new Fe centers, benefiting from charge modulation, can simultaneously adsorb two Hg atoms via charge transfer and orbital hybridization. The Fe3+-activated MoS2 exhibits strong resistance to SO2 and H2O, maintaining high Hg0 removal efficiency under a smelting gas atmosphere. This work reveals new configurations of Hg adsorption and provides a convenient route to design high-performance sorbents for heavy metal purification.

articles.title:
Photochemical
Interactions
of Nitrate Photolysis and
Photosensitization of BBOA: Enhanced HONO Production and the Formation
of Nitrophenols
articles.abstract: Abstract Renoxification of nitrate to reactive nitrogen species (RNS) can sustain atmospheric oxidant production. Because nitrate and light-absorbing brown carbon can coexist in biomass burning (BB) plumes, their photochemical interaction may alter RNS cycling. Furthermore, nitration of phenols in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) can form nitrophenols, potentially increasing the warming effect of aged BBOA. Yet the mechanisms of renoxification and nitration in irradiated nitrate-BBOA mixtures remain poorly understood. We experimentally investigate these coupled processes over a wide range of fir-wood BBOA concentrations during aqueous nitrate photolysis (10 mM) under acidic conditions using H2SO4. At low BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– ≤ 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), the steady-state production rate of HONO (Pss_HONO) increased as BBOA concentration increased, reaching a maximum enhancement factor of 1.8 driven primarily by triplet-mediated photosensitized reduction of NO2 to HONO. At higher BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– > 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), Pss_HONO progressively decreased and was nearly fully suppressed at TOCBBOA/NO3– = 0.7 mg L–1/mg L–1. This inhibition is attributed to reactions of aqueous HNO2/NO2 with phenols, accompanied by formation of nitrophenols. These findings point to a potentially overlooked daytime HONO source and an atmospheric source of nitrophenols, a key class of BrC chromophores, via photochemical interactions between nitrate photolysis and photosensitization of BBOA.

articles.title:
Submarine Groundwater
Discharge Acts as a Significant
Vector for Coastal Organophosphate Esters: Joint Evidence from Pollution
Surveys and Radionuclide Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous marine contaminants that raise global concern. While surface inputs are well-studied, the role of subsurface transport remains poorly constrained. Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) drives seawater-groundwater interactions, yet its impact on OPEs behavior remains overlooked. This study comprehensively investigates the distribution, transport property and sources of OPEs from coastal groundwater to seawater in the Beibu Gulf, China. No statistically significant difference in Σ19OPEs levels was found between groundwater and tidal flat porewater, while both matrices exhibited significantly higher levels than seawater. The high compositional similarity, strong correlations (p < 0.01) and PCA overlap of OPEs in different waters, as well as their shared source profiles indicated the transport potential of OPEs from groundwater to seawater. Multiple statistical modeling integrating OPEs, environmental factors and DOM components reveals the land-to-sea transport pathways and biogeochemical processes of OPEs via SGD. Furthermore, radon isotope analysis verified the presence of SGD, offering evidence for SGD-mediated OPE transport. For the first time, this work integrates pollutant investigation, multiple statistical analysis, and radionuclide tracing, to identify SGD as a previously underestimated vector of coastal OPEs and elucidates its potential transport mechanisms, providing crucial support for integrated land-sea management and risk assessment.

articles.title:
Aqueous
Carbonyl-Amino Aggregation Drives Atmospheric
Nitrogen-Containing Oligomer Formation in China Haze
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs) are ubiquitous in the troposphere and contribute to the reactive nitrogen cycle and aerosol light absorption, yet their formation mechanisms remain unclear, especially in polluted regions. Here, we characterized NOCs in PM2.5 during winter haze in the North China Plain (NCP), with a comparison to those in the Sichuan Basin (ScB). Reduced-nitrogen NOCs (Re-NOCs) accounted for 40% of organics detected in the ESI+ mode, highlighting their importance within atmospheric NOCs. Compared to dry haze (DH) in NCP, high-molecular-weight (HMW, m/z > 250) Re-NOCs in humid haze (HH) were enhanced, which positively correlated with NH4+ and the mass ratio of aqueous-phase secondary organic aerosols to total water-soluble organic aerosols, along with increases in aliphatic chain length and molecular unsaturation, indicating carbonyl-amino-driven oligomerization and cyclization. Aliphatic Re-NOCs dominated the Re-NOCs during HH, together with strong correlations of a typical NOC oligomer (C8H13N3O2) with water-soluble organic nitrogen and HMW Re-NOCs, further suggesting oligomerization as a key formation pathway for NOCs. We found that stronger aerosol acidity and higher temperature favored oligomerization of Re-NOCs compared to cyclization, resulting in enhanced C8H13N3O2 in ScB relative to that in NCP. Our work revealed oligomerization as a critical mechanism shaping the NOC composition, particularly HMW species.

articles.title:
Atmospheric
Concentrations and Emissions of Major
HFCs at Six Background Stations in China during 2012–2023
articles.abstract: Abstract In this study, a long-term atmospheric observation of HFC-23, -32, -125, -134a, -143a, and -152a was conducted at six background stations across China from 2011 to 2023. Using a tracer ratio method with HCFC-22 as the reference, emissions from four main economic regions, Northeast Plain (NEP), North China Plain (NCP), Yangtze River Delta (YRD), and Central South China (CSC), were estimated, and their trends were analyzed over four phases: Phase 1 (2012–2016), Phase 2 (2017–2018), Phase 3 (2019–2020), and Phase 4 (2021–2023). The results show that from 2011 to 2023, the atmospheric mixing ratios of all studied HFCs except HFC-152a exhibited increasing trends. Nationally, emissions of HFC-23 show a decreasing tendency during Phase 4, while emissions of HFC-32, -125, -134a, and -143a continued to rise throughout Phases 3 and 4. These four HFCs were identified as the dominant species, accounting for over 76% of total HFCs’ mass emissions. From Phase 3 to Phase 4, CO2-equivalent HFC emissions per capita increased slightly, whereas emissions per unit GDP decreased, which is mainly attributable to significant HFC reductions in the CSC region. Nevertheless, China’s average HFC emission intensities (whether calculated per unit GDP or per capita) remain approximately 1.5–1.6 times the global average.

articles.title:
Analysis of the
Potential Mediating Role of Plasma
Proteins in the Association Between Air Pollution Exposure and Lung
Cancer Risk Among Ever-Smokers
articles.abstract: Abstract The biological mechanisms linking air pollution to lung carcinogenesis remain underexplored. This study aimed to identify key proteins and pathways involved in mediating the effects of air pollutants on lung cancer risk. We analyzed 95 matched lung cancer case–control pairs of ever-smokers with prediagnosis plasma protein profiles measured in the Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort. We assessed associations between protein levels and six individual air pollutants, air pollution mixture, and lung cancer risk, adjusting for confounders and multiple testing. We identified overlapping proteins and enriched pathways associated with both exposures and lung cancer risk, followed by an exploratory high-dimensional mediation analysis (HIMA) to investigate the potential mediating roles of proteins. Seventeen proteins were associated with both exposures and lung cancer, including CX3CL1, ADAM15, and CXCL17 (P < 0.05). HIMA identified six proteins, including CX3CL1 and CXCL17, as potential mediating proteins of individual pollutant-lung cancer associations (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.05), while these findings did not remain significant when excluding cases diagnosed within one year of blood draw. The exploratory results suggest that proteins and pathways related to inflammatory chemokine signaling, immune modulation, and altered cell proliferation, migration, and survival may play significant roles in air pollution-lung cancer association among ever-smokers.

articles.title:
Kinetics of CO2 Hydrate Formation and Chemical-Potential-Driven
Dissociation in Porous Media
articles.abstract: Abstract Gas hydrates can form when water and a guest gas coexist within the hydrate stability field. Gas hydrates in porous rocks block flow fields. During CO2 storage in depleted reservoirs, pressure reduction and Joule–Thomson cooling may place near-well regions within the CO2 hydrate stability zone, raising concerns about injectivity loss. Hydrate stability is commonly inferred from the bulk pressure–temperature (P–T) phase diagram, which neglects flow and gas humidity transport under sustained flow. Using time-resolved optical microscopy in a “fish-bone” micromodel at fixed P and T, we find that injecting low-humidity CO2 produces a pore-scale cycle of hydrate formation and dissociation. The hydrate nucleates along gas–water–solid contact lines and grows by consuming CO2 dissolved in trapped pore water and then slows as CO2 supply becomes diffusion-limited through the hydrate layer. Despite constant bulk P and T, the low humidity of the injected CO2 extracts water as vapor, creating a water chemical potential deficit at the gas–hydrate interface and driving an inlet-to-outlet dissociation front. These results show that hydrate persistence under flow depends on pore-scale transport and gas-side water chemical potential and cannot be inferred from bulk P–T stability conditions alone.

articles.title:
OH-Initiated Heterogeneous
Reactions of Novel Organophosphate
Esters: Insights into Oxidation Chemistry and Atmospheric Persistence
articles.abstract: Abstract Novel organophosphate esters (OPEs), formed through chemical transformation of commercial antioxidants, are emerging contaminants with widespread environmental occurrence and potential health effects. Despite their widespread detection, the atmospheric reactivity, persistence, and transformation of novel OPEs remain unknown. Here, the heterogeneous OH oxidation of two surface-bound novel OPEs [tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (TDtBPP) and triisodecyl phosphate (TiDeP)] was explored by investigating the reaction kinetics and chemical mechanisms. The measured heterogeneous rate constants for TDtBPP and TiDeP were (2.81 ± 0.12) × 10–12 and (1.99 ± 0.16) × 10–12 cm3 molecules–1 s–1, respectively, equivalent to atmospheric lifetimes of up to 6.3 and 9.0 days. These lifetimes are significantly longer than previously predicted values (<1 day), suggesting that they are much more persistent in air than predicted. Based on UPLC-HRMS measurements, 22 transformation products from the heterogeneous reactions were identified for the first time. Analysis of atmospheric particle samples from two megacities in China identified four TDtBPP transformation products, demonstrating that the oxidation chemistry can occur under genuine environmental conditions. In-silico hazard screening further indicated that many transformation products may be more bioaccumulative and more toxic than the parent novel OPEs. The results not only provide new insights into the atmospheric persistence of novel OPEs but also underscore the significance of considering atmospheric transformation in the risk assessment of these emerging contaminants.

articles.title:
Associations
of PM2.5 and Its Oxidative
Potential with Childhood Allergy-Related Symptoms: A Cross-Sectional
Study in Guangdong Province, China
articles.abstract: Abstract Evidence linking PM2.5 exposure to allergic symptoms remains limited and inconsistent, partly because most studies rely on mass-based metrics alone. We conducted a population-based study among 131,346 children aged 6–18 years in six cities of Guangdong, China, to compare associations of PM2.5 mass concentration, oxidative potential (OP), and chemical components (metals, carbonaceous components, and ions) with rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis, and eczema symptoms. OP was assessed using the dithiothreitol assay and expressed as volume-normalized (DTTv) and mass-normalized (DTTm) metrics. PM2.5 mass and OP were generally positively associated with the three allergy-related symptoms. OP, particularly DTTm, provided more consistent and robust evidence of associations across outcomes than PM2.5 mass, supported by lower AIC/BIC values and greater stability in two-pollutant models. Single-component and mixture analyses indicated that multiple PM2.5 constituents contributed to allergy-related symptoms, and OP may partly explain the associations of Co, OC, Cu, and Hg, with the largest estimated indirect proportion reaching 36.2% for OC and rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms through DTTm. These findings suggest that OP captures health-relevant characteristics beyond particle mass and may serve as a complementary exposure indicator for understanding childhood symptoms of allergic diseases.
